high_consensus.description: Real operational gap. With runtime-critical changes in S2 and downstream dependency chains, lacking rollback criteria per sprint is risky. Actionable and low-to-moderate doc effort with high incident-response ROI.

High-value governance improvement. Explicit sprint exit gates prevent boundary bleed, enforce dependency integrity, and make 'independently shippable' verifiable. Very actionable and worth standardizing.
Strong acceptance-clarity improvement. Referencing unnamed invariants creates avoidable ambiguity; inlining or appending them makes AC-S2.5 directly testable with minimal effort.
Useful quality hardening. CI latency assertions without environment/method specs are prone to flake and dispute. Adding harness and statistical details is actionable and improves signal quality.

Near-critical observability gap. Test-time gates are insufficient for rollout decisions and deprecation follow-through; production metrics are needed for cycle-100 decisions. Moderate implementation cost, high operational value.

disputed.description: Critical correctness issue. Concurrent startup race behavior for merged-aliases regeneration is a high-risk path and should be explicitly acceptance-tested. Highly actionable and high ROI.
Low-value process optimization in this context. Per-sprint subagent/inline strategy documentation is optional and unlikely to materially improve delivery versus the added planning overhead.

blockers.concern: Atomic write via `rename(2)` fails across filesystem boundaries
blockers.why_matters: T2.4 specifies using a tempfile and `rename(2)` for atomic writes. If the temp directory (e.g., `/tmp`) and the target directory (`.run/`) reside on different filesystem mounts, `rename(2)` will throw an EXDEV error, completely breaking config generation.
blockers.recommendation: Ensure the tempfile is created in the exact same directory as the target file (`.run/`) before performing the `rename(2)` operation.

blockers.concern: Cross-runtime parity (Python, Bash, TS) is a massive technical debt trap
blockers.why_matters: Implementing the exact same 6-stage resolution algorithm and endpoint validation in three different languages (Python, Bash, TypeScript) guarantees future drift. Every future feature or bugfix will require triplicated effort and byte-for-byte parity testing.
blockers.recommendation: Consolidate the core resolution and validation logic into a single compiled binary (e.g., Rust/Go) or a single Python daemon that Bash and TS clients call via IPC/sockets.

blockers.concern: Cross-runtime parity (bash/python/TS) is a hidden complexity multiplier that may create chronic drift and flaky CI.
blockers.why_matters: Three implementations of resolver/validator/redactor increase maintenance burden and make subtle behavior mismatches likely, threatening deterministic guarantees.
blockers.recommendation: Reduce duplicated logic via single canonical engine or generated runtime bindings, and add contract/property tests that run on every change touching shared semantics.

blockers.concern: Known tooling instability (`Beads UNHEALTHY`) plus repeated `git commit --no-verify` creates governance and quality-control blind spots.
blockers.why_matters: Skipping local verification increases probability of broken commits, security regressions, and inconsistent sprint tracking/auditability.
blockers.location: Cycle constraints inherited from PRD/SDD (R-5), Risk Register R-5
blockers.recommendation: Require server-side mandatory checks for all protected branches, add temporary pre-push verification scripts, and prioritize tooling recovery as a tracked blocker task.

blockers.concern: Migration strategy combines strict-mode expansion, backward compatibility, and one-cycle deprecation windows without a full rollback/data-recovery plan.
blockers.why_matters: Operator configs may partially migrate, pass schema, but still resolve incorrectly; one-cycle windows can be too short for downstream adopters.
blockers.location: Sprint 2 T2.2/T2.9, Sprint 3 T3.4/T3.6, AC-S2.3, FR-3.7 exception notes
blockers.recommendation: Add versioned migration checkpoints, automated backup/restore of config files, and extend compatibility support until telemetry shows safe adoption thresholds.

blockers.concern: Process depends on single-operator synchronous decisions at critical path (Sprint 4 gate, scope approvals, fallback decisions).
blockers.why_matters: Any operator unavailability or delayed review can stall releases, leave deprecations half-applied, or force risky default decisions.
blockers.location: Sprint 4 T4.4 gate review, Operator-availability risk, cycle constraints requiring operator decisions
blockers.recommendation: Define delegated approvers, asynchronous decision SLA, and deterministic default behavior with rollback if gate review is missed.

blockers.concern: Reliance on `git commit --no-verify` bypasses critical safety checks
blockers.why_matters: The plan mandates `--no-verify` due to 'Beads UNHEALTHY (#661)'. Bypassing pre-commit hooks while simultaneously introducing strict schema validations, drift gates, and security redactors means developers will easily commit broken or unredacted code, defeating the CI/CD pipeline's first line of defense.
blockers.location: Executive Summary -> Cycle constraints inherited from PRD/SDD
blockers.recommendation: Fix the Beads workspace issue (Sprint 0) before starting Cycle-099, or implement a lightweight pre-commit hook fallback that enforces the new drift and schema gates without relying on the broken Beads environment.

blockers.concern: Security controls for operator-defined endpoints rely heavily on validation logic that may be bypassed via edge-case URL/DNS behavior.
blockers.why_matters: If SSRF or trust-boundary bypass occurs, attacker-controlled endpoints could exfiltrate metadata/secrets or pivot through internal networks.
blockers.recommendation: Add explicit TOCTOU mitigation requirements (resolve+connect verification), deny redirects by default, enforce strict host/IP pinning per request, and include adversarial fuzzing for URL parser discrepancies.

blockers.concern: Synchronous DNS rebinding checks will violate the 50ms latency budget
blockers.why_matters: Performing DNS resolve-and-verify at request time (T2.11) introduces network I/O into the critical path of model invocation. DNS queries can easily exceed 50ms, especially in degraded network environments, violating the NFR-Perf-1 p95 <= 50ms requirement.
blockers.recommendation: Implement an asynchronous DNS caching layer with background refresh, or perform the rebinding check only at configuration load time with a TTL-based invalidation.

blockers.concern: Timeline is overly compressed for the declared scope (4 sprints, 49 tasks, ~160 tests, multiple new CI workflows) with no buffer week.
blockers.why_matters: A single delayed large sprint (especially Sprint 1 or 2) cascades into blocked dependencies, forcing rushed quality gates or descope of core outcomes.
blockers.location: Executive Summary ("no buffer week"), Sprint Overview (S1/S2 marked LARGE), Success Metrics (5-6 weeks)
blockers.recommendation: Add explicit contingency capacity (10-20%), define must-ship vs deferable tasks per sprint, and pre-authorize a formal Sprint 2.5 buffer trigger with objective criteria.
